newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal and European Union sign fishing deal.
newsitem.headline: Senegal and European Union sign fishing deal.

text.p: Senegal and the European Union signed a new fishing deal on Wednesday, extending the life of the agreement for another four years.
"We have proved sitting around a table that we can overcome the toughest difficulties," Senegal's Minister for Fishing and Maritime Transport, Alassane Dialy Ndiaye, said at the signing ceremony.

The new agreement starting on May 1 will last four years instead of the previous two-year deal that ended last October. The two sides failed in November to agree the size of an EU compensation package in return for access to Senegalese fishing waters.
European vessels were asked to leave the West African country's waters.
The two sides finally struck a deal on Wednesday under which the EU will give Senegal 12 millions Ecus ($10.4 million) a year compared with nine million Ecus in the previous protocol.
Senegal had demanded 18 million Ecus and the EU had offered 10 million Ecus.
For the first time the new agreement stressed the need for periodic, month-long "biological respites" for Senegalese waters.
"I think it is a good and balanced agreement for both Senegal and the European Union," Emilio Mastracchio, head of the EU delegation, said.
Under the new agreement 148 European fishing vessels will be allowed to fish in Senegalese territorial waters.
The West African state earned more that 137 billion CFA francs ($242.5 million) from its fishing industry in 1995. More than 400,000 people are directly or indirectly dependent on the sector.
Senegal was in 1979 the first country to sign such a fishing protocol with the EU.
